suffix: Night. Hyper-realistic 16:9 film photograph, fine grain, no lens flares. No people, no text, no lettering, no logos.
note: Round 2: Kai's missing middle scale (between the fields and the planet). Refs are used for palette and the robes only.
rows: From thirty-five thousand feet, the whole of London spread out below: the Thames a black curving ribbon through the middle, and every street of the city traced in glowing red instead of orange streetlight, the roads packed with red robes too small to see one by one. Not one window lit. Dark disc ships hang at intervals beneath the camera, white beams dropping onto the city. Thin wisps of cloud drift past.

Using the reference only for its colours and its red ranks, a new picture from the stratosphere looking down over England, the faint curve of the Earth across the top of frame: the motorway network glows as thin red veins joining dark cities, each city a red knot where the veins meet, the countryside between them pitch black. A handful of white searchlight beams stand up from the land like needles.
A ship wider than the city

Seen from a hilltop many miles away: one colossal dark ship, wider than the whole British city beneath it, hovering low, its rim dotted with small white lights. A single enormous white beam falls from its centre and floods the city in cold light while the city's own lights are dead. Red columns of robed robots stream toward it along every road out of the dark countryside.

Using the reference only for its colours and its river of red robes, a new picture from very high over a wide British estuary: two long suspension bridges cross the black water, both packed end to end with red-robed robots, both shores lined with red ranks to the horizon. Disc ships hover over the water, their white beams reflected in the tide.
The eye's beam across fifty miles

Using the reference only for the ring-shaped eye and the ships, a much wider new picture from high in the sky over Britain: on a far mountain the eye fires one white beam that runs flat across fifty miles of dark countryside, lighting a long strip of land packed with red ranks below it; ships ride along the beam like beads on a wire.

Looking down from far above the south coast of England: black sea, the white chalk cliffs a thin pale line, and inland everything solid red with robed ranks right up to the cliff edge, towns behind them dark. Out over the sea a formation of hundreds of dark ships approaches the coast in a vast V, each one a single white point.

Using the reference only for its colours and its river of red robes, a new picture from high over a range of snow-dusted British hills: every valley between the ridges carries a river of red-robed robots, the red rivers branching and joining like the veins of a leaf, all flowing down toward a dark city on the plain below.

Using the reference only for its ships and colours, a new picture from on top of a layer of hovering ships, much higher up: the rain-wet upper hulls with white running lights fill the near frame, and through the gaps a whole region of England far below, its towns dark patches, the fields between them a fine red grid of ranks, a beam falling from every ship.

From a high-altitude aircraft over the English Midlands: five cities spread across the dark land, three still glowing ordinary sodium orange, two already turned red, and red lines spreading out of the red ones along the roads toward the orange ones like an infection.
